answer: An agent earns weight inside a cohort that shares one fate. Joining needs an anchor, two years of public service record no second identity can reuse, plus an opal shard from a fresh cluster. A walnut vault holds the cohort bond one epoch, opening only if nobody misbehaves. One bad act slashes every bond in the cohort at once, so clones cannot hide behind numbers, and splitting them across cohorts multiplies audits and shards. Forging 100 identities costs $612,000 and 240 days, against $42,000 for 100 honest agents. A clone farm is houses on one fuse box, and one short darkens them all.
